messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — noticed a fairness regression in canary-6 after the kernel selector change. short-request tail is getting starved by long sequences, looks like continuous batcher is favoring long-path kernels and holding mini-batches until long seqs join.
Maya: ugh. timeline? reproducible?
Alex: started ~1719780000, spike in short_queue_depth and p95 for <64 token requests. kv hit rate dipped too which is weird. can repro locally with mixed trace. here's a minimal reproducer: 
```bash
# send mix of short and long sequences
for i in {1..200}; do
  if (( i % 5 == 0 )); then
    curl -s -X POST $INFER_URL -d '{"input": "long..."}' &
  else
    curl -s -X POST $INFER_URL -d '{"input": "hi"}' &
  fi
done
```
and the scheduler config we used in Canary-6: 
```json
{"batcher": {"token_budget_target": "8000", "kernel_pref": "throughput", "soft_handshake": 0.0}}
```
Sam: telemetry confirms the pattern. short_queue_depth up x3, avg-mini-batch-size for long path went from 8->12, short path mini-batches dropped to 2 -> more preemption but fewer starts. kv_hit_rate -6pp. attaching concise log snip: 
```
[1719781234] batcher: formed batch id=aa size=12 kernels=matmul-v2 path=long
[1719781234] request short-id queued len=12 wait=420ms
[1719781235] kv: miss tenant=corp42 key=abc
```
Li: sounds like two coupled problems: 1) kernel selector bias toward long kernels because of throughput heuristic, 2) batch formation waits for long sequences to fill threshold before dispatching. propose a soft handshake that lets short requests claim fractional credits and get dispatched earlier. pseudocode: 
```python
# on enqueue
if req.len < SHORT_THRESH:
  credit = max(1, floor(token_budget_target * short_fraction))
else:
  credit = ceil(req.len * weight)
```
then allow fractional batching: small reqs can form micro-batches that still hit fast kernels.
Priya: agree on soft handshake. also think kernel selection needs a latency-aware override: prefer low-latency kernels (e.g., matmul-fastpath) for requests with len < 64 even if throughput degrades slightly. routing layer can tag short requests with prefer_fastpath=true.
Maya: can we quantify the tradeoff? need p95_short, fairness_index (short_throughput/long_throughput normalized), kv_hit_rate, and overall tokens/s. propose 1h canary A/B: control=current, exp=soft-handshake+short-pref.
Alex: propose parameters: soft_handshake=0.35, short_fraction=0.2, token_budget_target=7000, short_pref_weight=0.6. run at 5% traffic on cluster-alpha.
Li: I'll run the canary tonight. command I will use: 
```bash
rbctl rollout set canary --cluster=alpha --pct=5 \
  --set batcher.soft_handshake=0.35 \
  --set batcher.short_fraction=0.2 \
  --set batcher.token_budget_target=7000 \
  --set runtime.short_pref_weight=0.6
```
deploy-bot: :rocket: Canary rollout started for commit e3f2a9 on cluster-alpha (5% traffic).
Sam: quick after-10m snapshot (prelim): p95_short went from 220ms -> 180ms, fairness_index from 0.62->0.85, total tokens/s -2.8%, kv_hit_rate -1pp. short_queue_depth back to baseline.
Maya: nice improvement on short tail, small token loss looks acceptable. can we confirm stability at 1h and check regressions for high-concurrency tenants?
Li: will collect flamegraphs + trace ids. please tag any tenant you want excluded from canary if sensitive.
Priya: one more thought — if we implement short-pref, we should add a tiny warmup penalty for long sequences to avoid oscillation: when kernel switch happens, require 1-second stabilizer before flipping kernel for that lane. reduces churn.
Alex: good call. add stabilizer=1s to experiment. Li, Sam — follow up with perf traces and a quick diff of kernel selection counts (matmul-fastpath vs matmul-v2) by seq_len bucket.
Sam: will upload perf table in #eng-runtime later today.
Maya: sched a 30m sync tomorrow 11:30 am to review results — meeting invite: https://meet.link/shortlong-review
Alex: thanks all. main action items: run canary (Li), collect traces/metrics (Sam), add stabilizer tweak (Priya). ping here when done. :thumbsup:
